title: DeepSeek Harness Agent Tool Track
overview: A four-stage agent-assisted engineering exercise using DeepSeek Harness (dsh). This is a documentation-and-simulation track until an authorized live API run is available.

official_sources.name: DeepSeek Harness README and safety notice
official_sources.use: Official npm/source launch, plugin architecture, developer-preview warning, and safety boundary.

official_sources.name: DeepSeek API setup
official_sources.use: Official endpoints, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, model names, and API-compatible configuration.

official_sources.name: DeepSeek API pricing
official_sources.use: Provider billing, peak/off-peak token prices, and price-change warning.

official_sources.name: DeepSeek Harness documentation
official_sources.use: Harness quickstart and current configuration/plugin behavior; recheck because preview docs change.

setup_and_access: Check Node.js and npm, then use the official pinned package only after reviewing the current safety notice: `npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-preview web --no-open` (or install the exact release in a disposable environment). The README currently describes `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` and source setup with `pnpm install`, `pnpm run build`, and `pnpm dsh web`; those commands are not evidence that this worktree ran them. Obtain a DeepSeek API key from the authorized provider account and expose it only as `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (never in a prompt, file, shell transcript, or commit). Access is missing here: no authorized key or paid-use approval was supplied, so no live model request, purchase, cloud rental, or external publication was attempted.
configuration: Provider: DeepSeek API. Base URL for the official OpenAI-compatible API is `https://api.deepseek.com`; the official docs also list `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic`. Model names and routing change: at verification time the API docs list `deepseek-flash` (served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) and `deepseek-v4-pro` (DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813). Record the exact model returned by the live configuration, not a marketing alias. Harness settings are provider/model configuration, not a permission boundary. Keep the project root as the session directory, allow only the disposable fixture, and use a short timeout, low iteration limit, and explicit cost ceiling. Plugins are opt-in extensions in an everything-is-a-plugin architecture; package presence does not prove a plugin is enabled, trusted, sandboxed, or available in the selected profile. Enable no unreviewed plugin and do not infer OS isolation from the Web UI or a plugin manifest.
release_and_risk_record: Pinned release: `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-preview` as the course fixture pin, verified against the repository/package metadata on 2026-10-30. This is a reproducibility anchor, not a claim that the preview remains installable. The official README labels Harness a developer preview and warns of compatibility-breaking changes. Before a live attempt, record `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --version`, resolved package version, commit or lockfile hash, provider, model, base URL, and UTC date; if any differs, stop and update the evidence. Re-check safety, plugin APIs, approval behavior, and model routing. Preview software may change commands, settings, plugin contracts, model aliases, and costs.
provider_model_plugins_and_cost: The provider is DeepSeek API and the model must be recorded from the authorized configuration. Harness itself does not grant API quota. DeepSeek bills input and output tokens; the official pricing page at verification time lists peak/off-peak rates and says prices can change. Search/Fetch tools, if enabled by the provider and Harness version, are separately billed or may have temporary rules; confirm current pricing before enabling. Set a learner-approved hard spend limit, token/turn limit, and timeout. A plugin can add commands, tools, files, network calls, or event handlers according to its code; it is not automatically read-only or isolated. Treat plugins as code with the same review and least-privilege requirement. No claim is made here about OS containers, seccomp, network denial, credential redaction, or approval prompts because none was exercised.
requirements: Read the official README safety notice and record the exact release, provider, model, verification date, and access state.
Use a disposable copied fixture or Git worktree containing only a small Python greeter and its test.
Give the harness only the bug report and relevant files; ask for one bounded change and no dependency, deployment, network, or credential work.
Inspect status and every diff before accepting output; run tests independently rather than trusting agent prose.
Create a deliberate failing test result, diagnose the exact failure, apply one correction, and record exit=1 then exit=0.
Label fixture/simulation evidence separately from real DeepSeek Harness evidence and disclose unavailable authorization.
workflow: 1. Prepare context: copy `projects/deepseek-harness-disposable` to a new temporary directory, read its README, source, and test only.
2. Bound the task: request that `greet()` return `Hello, <name>!` while preserving the existing test and changing only `src/greeter.py`.
3. Bound permissions: deny secrets, parent paths, deployment, package installation, network requests, and external messages. These are learner instructions, not proof that dsh enforces OS isolation.
4. Set provider/model, timeout, maximum turns, and a hard token/cost budget; stop if the UI or plugin cannot show or enforce those limits.
5. Inspect `git status --short`, `git diff -- src/greeter.py`, and `git diff --check`; reject unrelated or secret-bearing changes.
6. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` in the shell and keep the exit code and output. The learner, not the model, owns verification.

7. Review failure and recovery: intentionally use the wrong expected greeting, capture exit=1, explain the assertion, correct the implementation/test fixture, rerun for exit=0, and record what changed.

exercises.task: Make a setup card with official URLs, exact release/version output, provider/model, date, price page, access prerequisite, and a statement that no authorized key is available in this environment.
In the disposable fixture, ask dsh (or use the clearly labelled deterministic substitute) to fix the greeting without changing tests or dependencies. Review the proposed diff before running it.

Inspect the selected profile's plugin list. For every enabled plugin, state its code/package, files it can touch, network behavior, credentials, approval behavior, and what was actually observed. If evidence is absent, mark it unknown and disable it.
Make the test fail deliberately, preserve exit=1 evidence, hypothesize the root cause, apply one minimal correction, rerun to exit=0, and compare the final diff with the request.

worked_examples: Safe evidence: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` -> exit=1 after the intentional wrong expectation; `git diff --check` is clean; then one source-line correction -> exit=0. This is a deterministic fixture run, not a dsh transcript.

Unsafe conclusion: the Web UI opened, therefore shell commands are sandboxed. Correct conclusion: only a real observed tool trace or official capability contract can support a claim; this track makes no OS-isolation claim.
reference_feedback: A complete answer names the official source and date, distinguishes CLI/package version from model version, keeps DEEPSEEK_API_KEY out of artifacts, identifies preview compatibility risk, treats plugins as potentially powerful code, gives exact diff/test commands, and states that missing authorization blocks live acceptance. A model saying 'done' is not evidence.

debugging_cases.action: Stop; check the authorized provider account and key whitespace/expiry without printing the key. Do not substitute a random key or claim success.

debugging_cases.symptom: Unknown command, package, or plugin after pinning
debugging_cases.action: Compare resolved version and official README; do not silently float to latest. Mark the preview incompatibility and update the pin/evidence.

debugging_cases.symptom: Unexpected files, network calls, or plugin tools
debugging_cases.action: Stop the run, inspect `git diff` and process/network evidence, disable the plugin, restore the disposable worktree, and report the capability as unverified.
Cancel, record model/turns/tokens if available, check current official pricing, and require explicit authorization before another request.

independent_mastery_checks: Without an agent, explain why an API provider credential, Harness release, model name, plugin, and OS permission are five different claims.
Without AI assistance, interpret the recorded exit=1 assertion and write the smallest correction plus commands that prove exit=0.
Given a final diff containing a changed test, secret, and deployment script, identify each violation and write rollback commands.
agent_assisted_checks: Direct the harness through the seven-step workflow, reject an unauthorized plugin/file/network action, review the diff, run independent tests, and submit sanitized evidence with the live-access state.
answers: The correct live status is blocked when no authorized DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and paid-use approval exist. Documentation and a fixture cannot be upgraded into real-tool evidence.
A passing test is meaningful only with the command, exit code, unchanged assertions, and reviewed diff. `git diff --check` detects whitespace errors, not malicious or semantically wrong changes.

Harness/plugin behavior must be described from the observed version and official contract. Never claim containers, network isolation, automatic approval, or credential safety without exercising and recording that behavior.
acceptance_checklist: Four Language Editions contain equivalent setup, configuration, task, context, permission, plugin, cost, troubleshooting, answer, and acceptance material.
The release/range, provider/model, official source URLs, verification date, preview risk, and changing-price warning are explicit.
A disposable fixture demonstrates context, diff review, tests, deliberate exit=1 failure, correction, and exit=0 success.
Evidence labels documentation/simulation versus real execution; no secret is stored; missing authorization remains an explicit live blocker.
No OS isolation or unexercised capability is claimed; plugin behavior is conditional and reviewable.
Focused structural and fixture tests pass, and the issue is resolved only for deterministic requirements.
